participants.name: Lynleit
participants.reading: Lynleit studies Kyrien first as a recruit whose failed attack nearly harmed her. Their card games make that scrutiny personal: she learns his tells and begins noticing his hands and breath. Later she attempts intimacy as a possible treatment for their shared curse, but remains interested after they survive without completing it. Mikhail's mock blessing exposes her family association with the Cult of Inanna. She counters with abstract principles and increasingly personal objections. His teasing does not create her attraction to Kyrien or make ancestry a reason for it. In the park, she wants to correct her private sense of failure, then finds satisfaction in knowing Kyrien as a particular person. Her theory follows an impulse already present. The preparation remains theoretical. Her attention shifts from proving competence toward learning his individual responses; the current park draft leaves that passage for the author rather than depicting it.

participants.name: Kyrien
participants.reading: Kyrien wants to beat Lynleit at cards and dislikes finding that she can read him. Her elegance and nerve also attract him. He stays because he wants the battle, then finds himself facing private questions that her orders cannot answer. After the attempted intimacy, she will not tell him why their curse disappeared. He notices her pleasure in success and answers with a joke rather than a declaration. When she later asks for his flask, he does not force an explanation. The author also intends him to notice how being able to affect him changes her confidence. This reciprocal observation is not a shift into generic dominance. Quiet companionship and private tells matter alongside practical dependence and protected secrets. Her initiative, pride, and curiosity can reach him, but both must gradually allow themselves to be affected rather than continually managing what the other notices. Their intimacy includes being quietly recognized, accompanied, and challenged without their usual defenses; restraint can become unnecessary without making them talkative.

pairs.dynamic: The interrogation, card games, protected secret, and voluntary decision to stay give this pairing different kinds of familiarity. In Doom Has an Address, an incomplete attempt at intimacy breaks the shared curse. Lynleit loses the excuse of treatment without losing her interest in Kyrien; he is left trying to understand what happened. Their sexual relationship begins later in Arc 1. Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge precede Doom. Months afterward, a spontaneous park encounter lets Lynleit's curiosity and wounded pride become a successful private milestone. Oral intimacy, reciprocal exploration, first intercourse, and pregnancy remain separate. The family theme does not turn ancestry into an instruction or make grief itself attraction. Lynleit bears their son during her disappearance and later keeps him hidden from both Kyrien and the wider world. They restore intimacy during Arc 2 and eventually conceive a second child, a daughter, who is born later. The daughter's conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2, not within it. The author has confirmed this direction, not the scenes that restore intimacy or the timing of Kyrien's discovery of their son. Duty remains primary; a second child does not substitute for the work of reconnection.

participants.name: Lynleit
participants.reading: Felix's flirting belongs to a long friendship she refuses to reorganize around his advances. Her ease with him, combined with the repeated refusal, creates visible chemistry without requiring matching sexual intent.

participants.name: Felix
participants.reading: Lynleit is one of the few people his charm cannot simply move into the response he wants. Familiar affection, physical ease, and repeated deflection keep his attraction active even when he respects the boundary she has made. He remains internally fixated on her while growing close to Sherie through work. Enjoying Sherie's company does not immediately change whom he imagines being intimate with; his attachment to Lynleit takes more than successful flirtation to loosen.

pairs.dynamic: The tension is easy for readers to recognize because it already has a social rhythm: he advances through jokes and flirtation, she ignores or redirects him, and neither abandons the closeness underneath the exchange. It does not need to become a relationship to remain real.

participants.name: Yulia
participants.reading: Hiyu irritates her into sustained attention. She keeps arguing, correcting, and following because his ideas have already occupied more of her mind than she wants to admit. Suppressed attraction can sharpen both her impatience and her awareness of his physical presence.

participants.name: Hiyu
participants.reading: Yulia is the critic whose resistance makes an idea worth pursuing. He becomes dependent on her attention before he understands that the dependence is personal, leaving him oblivious to tension that is already changing how he seeks her out.

pairs.dynamic: Their arguments repeatedly force proximity and attention. They lean over the same evidence, reach for the same document, and forget ordinary distance while trying to prove incompatible explanations. Yulia notices first and steps away; Hiyu continues the theory and wonders why she moved. Her anger becomes disproportionate when his recklessness makes the possibility of losing him real. Hiyu recognizes the bond through absence: an investigation without her corrections becomes less interesting, and he keeps turning toward the place where she should be. Yulia and Hiyu become intimate by learning to communicate through the noise they already create together.

participants.name: Kyrien
participants.reading: Sherie's charm is too deliberate to disarm him, but the precision behind it earns his attention. He is more likely to watch for the moment her performance fails than reward the performance itself.

participants.name: Sherie
participants.reading: Kyrien's refusal to be steered threatens a skill she has internalized as part of her identity. Each failed attempt to produce a reaction can make his eventual attention feel more valuable and personally dangerous.

pairs.dynamic: Sherie uses language and calibrated flirtation to control the rhythm of an exchange. Kyrien answers with silence, literalism, or no usable reaction at all. Repeated negotiation could turn her professional frustration into sexual tension without making them compatible or displacing Kyrien's eventual relationship with Lynleit.

participants.name: Fionn
participants.reading: Fionn's affection and desire for Helena are genuine. He separates bodily and domestic closeness from the secrets he believes he must carry alone, never understanding that this division changes what their intimacy means to her.

participants.name: Helena
participants.reading: Helena experiences desire alongside the need to be admitted into Fionn's complete life. Physical familiarity can therefore intensify resentment: she can be close enough to know his body while remaining excluded from the truth governing him.

pairs.dynamic: Their sexual tension survives inside a real marriage because attraction and grievance occupy the same private space. The closer they become physically, the harder it is for Helena to accept that Fionn still decides which parts of himself she is permitted to know.

participants.name: Natalia
participants.reading: Lester is the living exception that Natalia cannot finish classifying. Her professional attention can become personal before she recognizes the change, especially when he interrupts an examination by noticing that she is watching him rather than the phenomenon around him.

participants.name: Lester
participants.reading: Natalia's analytical distance gives Lester something unusually difficult to provoke. He enjoys forcing the reserved researcher into immediate experience, but the tension changes when he wants her attention to recognize the man rather than examine the demiholumn condition.

pairs.dynamic: Repeated cases bring Natalia's examination of Lester into conflict with his insistence on being treated as more than a case. He provokes her to act; she notices more than he expected. Their attraction does not answer her questions about his demiholumn nature. Neither knows how he came into existence. His chronology is intrinsically contradictory, not a solvable transformation history. Natalia's recognition that contradiction belongs to nature does not mean she can explain him completely or that attraction answers the contradiction.

participants.name: Sherie
participants.reading: Sherie enjoys directing an exchange, while Felix teases back and complicates her control. As their work repeatedly overlaps, she finds room to become theatrical, petty, ridiculous, or openly delighted without losing his respect. She may recognize their intimate potential before he does. His fixation on Lynleit can hurt despite his responsive attention; her confidence does not remove disappointment, boundaries, or doubt about whether he sees her clearly. She gradually recognizes the seriousness beneath his jokes and becomes someone around whom he need not always entertain.

participants.name: Felix
participants.reading: Felix enjoys Sherie's company, answers her teasing, and gradually seeks her out while remaining internally fixated on Lynleit. His attention is responsive, but he may interpret Sherie's interest as habitual charm or their closeness as an entertaining professional friendship. Emotional investment can precede his recognition of its intimate possibility. His attachment to Lynleit has genuine weight and takes more than successful flirtation to loosen. Moving toward Sherie eventually means recognizing her own importance to him and wanting her without treating her as a substitute for Lynleit.

pairs.dynamic: They have no meaningful personal relationship at the story's opening. Sherie's diplomatic responsibilities increasingly overlap with Felix's work around Lynleit and MSF, bringing repeated encounters before either chooses closeness. Familiarity, respect, private jokes, and a compatible rhythm develop gradually. Her confident, playful dominance meets his expressiveness, improvisation, and willingness to challenge her. Humor, visible enjoyment, mutual provocation, and occasional reversals carry into affection and eventual adult intimacy. Care becomes particularly revealing when one stops performing and the other remains attentive. Readers can notice Felix building intimacy's foundations with Sherie while still imagining it with Lynleit; narration need not explain that contradiction. The later teasing challenge to Lynleit remains, but it neither starts their familiarity nor reduces Sherie's interest to winning him. This differs from Lynleit's strategic recruitment of Kyrien and their quieter recognition through restrained attention, protected secrets, and gradually accepted vulnerability. Both couples remain subplots beneath the political and supernatural story. The direction is confirmed; particular encounters, recognition, boundaries, and chronology remain unwritten.
